Free air under the diaphragm (pneumoperitoneum) means a perforated viscus.

glossary.GI: Gastrointestinal: the gut from mouth to anus.
glossary.rupture: A tear or burst through a structure.
glossary.duodenum: The first part of the small bowel, just after the stomach.
glossary.small bowel: The small intestine: duodenum, jejunum and ileum.
glossary.colon: The large bowel, between the caecum and the rectum.
glossary.peptic ulcer disease: Ulcers of the stomach or duodenum caused by acid damage to the lining.
glossary.trauma: Physical injury, such as from a crash, fall, stab or blow.
glossary.distension: Swelling of the abdomen from gas, fluid or dilated bowel.
glossary.collapse: Sudden loss of strength or consciousness, often from shock.
glossary.inflammatory markers: Blood tests such as WCC and CRP that rise with inflammation.
glossary.tachycardia: Heart rate above 100 beats per minute.
glossary.hypotension: Low blood pressure; here a late sign of shock.
glossary.late sign: A finding that only appears once the illness is advanced.
glossary.epigastric: The upper central abdomen, just below the breastbone.
glossary.generalised pain: Pain felt all over the abdomen rather than in one place.
glossary.bowel sounds: Gurgling noises from gut movement heard with a stethoscope; reduced in peritonitis.
glossary.WCC: White cell count; raised in infection and inflammation.
glossary.CRP: C-reactive protein, a blood marker of inflammation.
glossary.confusion: Muddled thinking, which in sepsis signals poor brain perfusion.
glossary.distal ileum: The last part of the small bowel, just before the caecum.
glossary.constipation: Infrequent or difficult passing of stool.
glossary.dopamine antagonist: A drug that blocks dopamine receptors; metoclopramide works this way to reduce nausea.
glossary.mechanical bowel obstruction: A physical blockage of the bowel, for example by adhesions, tumour or twisting.
glossary.CT: Computed tomography: a cross-sectional X-ray scan.
glossary.IV contrast: Dye given into a vein so vessels and organs show up on CT.
glossary.gold standard: The best available test for confirming a diagnosis.
glossary.specific: A specific test rarely gives a positive result in people who don't have the disease.
glossary.surgical emergency: A problem needing an operation without delay.
glossary.broad-spectrum antibiotics: Antibiotics that cover a wide range of bacteria, used before the organism is known.
glossary.resection: Surgical removal of part of an organ.
glossary.sigmoid: The S-shaped last part of the colon before the rectum.
glossary.colostomy: An opening of the colon onto the abdominal wall, with stool collected in a bag.
glossary.mucosal barrier: The protective mucus and lining cells that stop acid digesting the stomach wall.
glossary.acid-peptic digestion: Damage to the gut wall by stomach acid and the enzyme pepsin.
glossary.bile: Digestive fluid from the liver that irritates the peritoneum if it leaks.
glossary.chemical peritonitis: Peritoneal inflammation caused by acid or bile rather than bacteria.
glossary.bacterial peritonitis: Peritoneal inflammation caused by bacterial infection.
glossary.diaphragm: The dome-shaped muscle separating chest from abdomen.
glossary.free air: Gas outside the bowel in the peritoneal cavity, seen under the diaphragm on an erect film.
glossary.primary anastomosis: Joining the bowel ends together at the first operation.
glossary.contaminated field: An operating area soiled by faeces or pus, where joins heal badly.
glossary.systemic inflammatory response: Body-wide inflammation causing fever, fast heart rate and leaky vessels.
glossary.septic shock: Sepsis with low blood pressure despite fluids, needing vasopressors.
